newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil cuts IOF taxes on foreign investment-report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil cuts IOF taxes on foreign investment-report.

text.p: The Brazilian government has cut a host of financial transaction taxes on foreign investment, including a lowering of its tariff on fixed income accounts to two percent from seven percent, local news agency InvestNews said.

InvestNews, citing a Central Bank statement released to markets, said the tariff on all foreign loans to Brazilian borrowers, including Eurobonds, would be zero percent. It did not say what the previous tariff was.
The tariff on Annex Four accounts, which are mostly used in stock market investments, will remain zero, InvestNews said.

The tariff on non-resident accounts used to send money into Brazil from abroad, and on interbank operations between foreign and Brazilian banks authorized to operate in the foreign exchange market, will be cut to two percent from seven percent. Such transactions are carried out through so-called CC5 accounts.
The tax for investors in privatization funds will remain zero.
A Central Bank spokeswoman could not confirm the InvestNews report.
